occurrences.en: Your outline should smoothly conduct you from one point to the next, but do not permit it to railroad you.
occurrences.zh: 提纲应当顺畅地引导你从一个要点走向下一个，但不要让它反过来束缚你。

occurrences.en: Do not attempt to compose a perfectly correct draft the first time around.
occurrences.zh: 不要试图第一次就写出一份完全正确的初稿。

occurrences.en: Your pages will be easier to keep track of that way, and, if you have to clip a paragraph to place it elsewhere, you will not lose any writing on the other side.
occurrences.zh: 这样更容易整理各页；如果需要剪下一段放到别处，也不会因此丢掉纸张背面的文字。

occurrences.en: It's worth remembering, however, that though a clean copy fresh off a printer may look terrific, it will read only as well as the thinking and writing that have gone into it.
occurrences.zh: 不过值得记住的是，一份刚从打印机出来的整洁稿件看起来也许很漂亮，但它读起来究竟有多好，最终仍取决于其中投入的思考和写作质量。

occurrences.en: Once you have a first draft on paper, you can delete material that is unrelated to your thesis and add material necessary to illustrate your points and make your paper convincing.
occurrences.zh: 一旦初稿已经落在纸面上，你就可以删去与论点无关的材料，并补入说明观点、增强文章说服力所必需的内容。
